module: Define the release and assessment boundary

lesson.title: Separate permission from high-risk classification
lesson.summary: Separate classification, applicable scope and prohibited use.

prerequisites.reason: Classification attaches to the defined system and intended purpose. The prohibited-practice check needs the actual intended function and context.

blocks: **High-risk classification** identifies a legal route; it is not permission to use the system. Check Article 5 prohibitions separately, including each prohibition's conditions and exceptions. A conformity procedure cannot make a prohibited practice lawful.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(2), 5, 6(1)–(4), 43; Annexes I and III

blocks: Article 6(1) concerns a product or safety component covered by an Annex I law and subject to the specified third-party assessment condition. For **Annex I Section A**, the relevant product-law assessment route matters. Section A is a defined list, not every law regulating products.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(2), 5, 6(1)–(4), 43; Annexes I and III

blocks: For **Annex I Section B**, Article 2(2) limits which AI Act provisions apply; this course's ordinary Chapter III conformity pathway does not automatically apply. Record the particular sector regime rather than sending every Annex I product through the same checklist.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(2), 5, 6(1)–(4), 43; Annexes I and III

blocks: Article 6(2) covers the specified uses in **Annex III**. Article 6(3) can exclude certain listed systems when they pose no significant risk, including by not materially influencing decision-making, and meet a listed condition. Profiling natural persons remains high-risk. Providers relying on exclusion must document it and meet the relevant registration duty.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(2), 5, 6(1)–(4), 43; Annexes I and III

blocks: Northbridge's case stipulates material influence on applicant shortlisting, an Annex III employment use. Harbour's case stipulates a qualifying Section A medical-product route. Neither case determines the status of your actual product. Record unknown facts rather than treating an industry label as a completed classification.

options.blocks: Check the limited AI Act scope and the sector regime.
options.reason: Article 2(2) gives Section B a distinct boundary.

questions.prompt: An Article 5 practice is prohibited on the stated facts. Can a favourable assessment authorise it?

options.blocks: Yes, if the certificate is independently issued.
options.reason: Independence does not create an exception to Article 5.

options.blocks: Yes, once the system is registered.

options.reason: Classification and conformity do not supply permission to breach Article 5.
